# Signatories

This section provides the ISC with a view of the support received from
the community for a proposal. Acceptance isn't predicated on
popularity but community acceptance is important. Willingness to
accept outside input is also a good marker for project delivery.

An optional section would be for R-Core signatories where changes to R
are proposed.
-->

## Project team
<!--
Who are the people responsible for actually delivering the project if
the proposal gets accepted and are already signed up and rearing to
go? Briefly describe all participants and the skills they will bring
to the project. Include public artifacts such as code repositories to
show their tack record.
-->

dabestr is developed by the Claridge-Chang lab (ACCLAB) at Duke-NUS Medical School and collaborators, who authored the methods it implements and also maintain DABEST-Python and estimationstats.com. One primary developer (about 0.4 FTE over 9 months) will come from the existing maintainer team, with design review and statistical validation from the co-applicants at no cost to the grant.

Track record: github.com/ACCLAB/dabestr (CRAN), github.com/ACCLAB/DABEST-Python, estimationstats.com, and the two papers in References [@ho2019, @lu2026].

## Contributors
<!--
Who are the people who have actively helped with this proposal but

The authors of this proposal will all be on the core project team.
